land.text: 'Panchala was annexed into the Magadha empire during the reign of Mahapadma Nanda in the mid-4th century BCE'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Nanda Empire shape from -333 (1.56 M km2) holds the whole country; its first year is six years after the infobox's c. 340 BCE.

capitals.name: Kampilya (Kampil)
capitals.note: Capital of southern Panchala in the Mahabharata's division of the country 'into two territories'. Coordinates approximate and mine; Kampilya is not in the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Ahichchhatra
capitals.note: Capital of northern Panchala in the same division (near Bareilly). Coordinates approximate and mine; not in the gazetteer. The page does not say which was the main seat or when.

correction.text: Panchala: 'located in the Ganges-Yamuna Doab', 'the modern-day areas of Rohilkhand such as Bareilly', Budaun, Shahjahanpur, Farrukhabad, Kannauj, Kanpur, western Hardoi and 'the central Ganga-Yamuna Doab', 'to the west of the Gomti river, and the north of the Chambal River'

keyframe_review.note: -600..-451. The page gives no area. Cliopatria's 4,960 km2 disc (bbox 78.59-79.55E 27.74-28.51N, centroid 79.08E 28.12N, in Rohilkhand around Bareilly and Budaun) lies inside the country the page names; my correction (the gazetteer's Rohilkhand plus 70 km round Kannauj and 50 km round Kanpur, about 45,000 km2) is my reading of the district list, not a boundary the page draws. Parts of Lakhimpur and the rest of the Doab named on the page are left out.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria drops Panchala in -405, but the page keeps it until its annexation under Mahapadma Nanda 'in the mid-4th century BCE' (infobox span to 'c. 340 BCE'). Cliopatria's Shaishunaga shape for -404 holds none of the cells of Panchala's disc, and the Nanda shape from -333 does, so without this keyframe the land would be stateless from -404 to -334.

region.text: Panchala as 'one of the sixteen mahajanapadas of the c. 6th century BCE', northern Panchala at Ahichchhatra and southern at Kampilya

ledger.note: 600 BCE: Panchala enters the map as one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas. The page gives its infobox span as 'c. 1100 BCE - c. 340 BCE' and the Mahajanapada list to 'the c. 6th century BCE'; -600 is Cliopatria's first year, so the year is a bridge. Its Late Vedic phase (c. 1100-500 BCE) is not drawn.

340 BCE: Magadha under Mahapadma Nanda annexes Panchala. 'Panchala was annexed into the Magadha empire during the reign of Mahapadma Nanda in the mid-4th century BCE'; the infobox ends the span at 'c. 340 BCE'. The year is the infobox's; the page's text says only 'mid-4th century'.

certainty.note: The page bounds the country only by rivers and forest (west of the Gomti, north of the Chambal, the Ganga's source forests); no frontier with Kuru, Surasena or Kosala is given.

sources.title: Pañcāla
sources.note: Territory, two capitals, infobox c. 1100-c. 340 BCE, oligarchic by the 5th century, annexed under Mahapadma Nanda in the mid-4th century BCE.

notes: One page for two shapes. Not settled: (1) the end. The text says 'mid-4th century BCE' and the infobox c. 340 BCE, but its other infobox dates are garbled (c. 850, c. 750, c. 400 CE) and the same page describes the Gupta annexation, so c. 340 is read as the end of the Mahajanapada. Cliopatria's Nanda shape starts in -333, so -339..-334 is a gap if the Nanda dossier keeps that start. (2) The page names no war, so none is listed; the annexation by Mahapadma Nanda is undated within the mid-4th century. (3) Kuru, with which the page says Panchala was 'closely allied' in Late Vedic times, is janapada-of-kuru (other group); nothing territorial is dated. (4) Region names: Rohilkhand is in the gazetteer; Kampilya, Ahichchhatra (place) and Panchala (region) are not.
